headline: A 2014 law changes how two congressional gold medals are presented and says the medals should go to the Smithsonian for display and research.
what_it_does: The law lets the Speaker of the House and the President pro tempore of the Senate, instead of the President, present a gold medal on behalf of Congress to Martin Luther King Jr. and Coretta Scott King. It also lets the Speaker and the President pro tempore present a single gold medal honoring the Montford Point Marines for their World War II service. After each medal is awarded, it must be given to the Smithsonian Institution for display and research. Congress states that the Smithsonian should display the King medal, especially at the National Museum of African American History and Culture, and the Montford Point medal, especially at the National Museum of African American History and Culture or other related locations.
